methodology.heading: How Lens works
methodology.intro: Every bar, label and rating in Lens links here. This page explains how each is made and where it falls short.
methodology.draft: This page is a draft. Rater lists, validation results and the changelog are added before launch.

coverage.title: Coverage bar
coverage.body: The bar counts distinct outlets that covered a story, after merging copies of the same wire report. Each outlet counts once. We show the bar only when at least 4 outlets have covered the story; below that we say coverage is limited.

factuality.title: Factuality
factuality.body: Outlet factuality comes from named third-party raters. We show the rater, their method and the date for every rating. Outlets without a rating are shown as Not rated.

ownership.title: Ownership
ownership.body: Ownership is shown only with a link to evidence. Where we have no verified evidence, the owner is listed as Unknown.

blindspots.title: Blindspots
blindspots.body: A bias blindspot is a story where most rated outlets covering it sit on one side. A language blindspot is a story covered widely in one language and barely in another, for example Hindi and English.

summaries.title: How summaries are verified
summaries.body: Every summary sentence cites the articles it comes from. Quotes are checked word for word against the stored text, and a separate model checks that each cited article supports its sentence. We show Verified against sources only when both checks pass.

languages.title: Languages
languages.body: Headlines are always shown in their original language and script. Translated summaries are labeled with the language they were translated from.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: For most outlets we can only analyze headlines and short summaries, not full articles. Each story says when that is the case.

corrections.title: Corrections
corrections.body: If a story is grouped wrongly or a rating is out of date, report it. We review every report and record changes in the changelog.

bias.title: Outlet bias
bias.body: Each outlet carries a political-lean rating from a named third-party rater: Left, Center or Right. The coverage bar counts how many distinct outlets from each side covered a story. The rating describes the outlet, not the individual article, and outlets without a rating are shown as Not rated. We show the rater's exact wording (for example "Left-Center") on every article, and group leaning ratings with their side. Colors and patterns are chosen to avoid party colors.

editorial.title: Editorial ratings
editorial.body: Where no third-party rater covers an outlet, a few bias ratings come from the Lens editor's own judgment. They are labelled "Rated by Lens editor", marked low confidence, and have no published rubric or independent review yet. We replace them when a third-party rating becomes available.

signIn.title: Sign in to Lens
signIn.intro: Keep your preferences on every device you use.
signIn.what1: Saves your answer language, answer length, and the topics and states you follow.
signIn.what2: Builds your For you page from the topics you follow.
signIn.what3: Never changes which outlets appear in a story or an answer.
signIn.gets: Only an account number that Google makes for Lens. Not your email, name, photo or contacts. Lens stores it scrambled (hashed), so it can't be traced back to you.
signIn.consent: Signing in turns on personalization. You can delete everything, including your sign-in, at any time on the Preferences page.

me.title: Your preferences
me.intro: Lens works without an account. Sign in to keep your preferences on every device, or turn on personalization in this browser only. Lens remembers only what you choose here.
me.consentWhat: What Lens stores: the answer language, site language, topics and regions you follow, answer length and audio choice; the stories you open (to show what changed since your last visit) and the questions you ask Lens, both for {days} days.
me.consentNot: What Lens never stores: your name, email or phone; any political preference; which outlets or sides you read. What you follow never changes which outlets appear in a story or an answer.
me.consentNote: You can delete everything at any time.
me.audioLater: Audio summaries are not available yet.
me.retention: Opened stories and questions are deleted automatically after {days} days.
me.deleteConfirm: This deletes your preferences, opened stories and question history, and turns personalization off. Continue?
